name: AD8022
tagline: ADI's 130 MHz, 2.5 nV/√Hz XFCB bipolar dual. Head-Fi rollers say it out-resolves NJM4580 and nears an AD797.

lineage.note: Sole source on XFCB high-voltage bipolar. Datasheet Rev A 9/02, B 5/05, C 8/11.

part_numbers.note: 8-lead SOIC_N, lead-free. Stocked by RS, LCSC; ADI lifecycle unconfirmed.
8-lead MSOP, lead-free; LCSC stock. Reel suffixes -REEL/-REEL7 unconfirmed.
Legacy leaded SOIC code from older datasheets; probably obsolete.
Probable pre-RoHS MSOP code; never confirmed.

key_specs.value: +5 V single, or ±2.5 V to ±12 V
High output current; stable into capacitive loads

reputation.summary: Head-Fi 'Opamp thread' posters say swapping NJM4580 for AD8022 improved resolution and timbre, coming close to an AD797ANZ. They call it spatial, clear and transparent ('pure music') and say it can drive headphones directly. It needs careful decoupling, and high bias current suits low-impedance sources only. A niche forum reputation.
typical_uses: Direct headphone drive at modest levels (forum reports)
Low-impedance, low-noise preamp and ADC-driver stages
caveats: 130 MHz bandwidth: needs tight decoupling and short layout; can oscillate in socket adapters.
Relatively high input bias current: poor behind high-impedance sources or large feedback resistors.
SOIC / MSOP only; needs a DIP-8 adapter for socket rolling.

counterfeit_notes: No documented AD8022 counterfeits. Cheap multi-pack listings (e.g. Amazon 'AD8022ARZ AD8022AR SOP-8') are of unknown origin. Buy from authorised distributors; remarked SOIC audio duals are common.

silicon_changes.summary: ASE Chungli, Taiwan added as an assembly subcontractor for 8- and 10-lead MSOP to secure supply. AD8022 MSOP variants are reportedly listed. Die and datasheet unchanged.
silicon_changes.identification: ASE Chungli parts carry a backside tool or laser mark 'TAIWAN' (country of origin); otherwise use a date code after the PCN effective date.

spec_deltas.after: existing site(s) plus ASE Chungli, Taiwan

silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: assembly site added; same die and datasheet.
silicon_changes.verification: PCN content and Rev. -, A, B forms confirmed; AD8022ARMZ listing reported but not directly seen.

silicon_changes.summary: PCN 10_0339 has an attachment 'AD8022ARMZ Marking Change' / 'Marking Comparison', showing the MSOP top mark changed. Reason and any other changes unknown. No die change indicated.
silicon_changes.identification: Old and new top marks are shown in ADI's marking-comparison attachment; the marking text itself has not been read.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: marking only; matters when identifying genuine or older stock.
silicon_changes.verification: ADI-hosted attachment found; PCN text not retrieved (unrelated PCN 20_0339 came up instead). Scope unconfirmed.

silicon_changes.summary: PCN 26_0028 qualifies ADI Limerick, Ireland (ADLK) as a wafer fab for XF26/XF18/XF12/XF8 process products. One source listed AD8022ARMZ and reel variants; a second check did not confirm it.
silicon_changes.identification: No marking change. Trace by ADI lot or date code against the PCN effective date.

spec_deltas.before: previous fab for XF-process products (not named)

silicon_changes.audio_impact: None documented; ADI states no fit, form, function or reliability impact.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: same design and datasheet per ADI; AD8022 listing unconfirmed.
silicon_changes.verification: PCN scope confirmed; AD8022 inclusion seen only once and unconfirmed.

UChicago EDG mirror holds REV. A (https://edg.uchicago.edu/~bogdan/ADC_QUIET/DOC/parts/AD8022.pdf)
2.5 nV/√Hz @100 kHz, 1.2 pA/√Hz, 130 MHz, 50 V/µs, 68 ns, 4.0 mA/amp, XFCB (https://www.analog.com/en/products/ad8022.html)
Supply +5 V or ±2.5 V to ±12 V; SOIC_N and MSOP (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ad8022.pdf)

Technology now names the XFCB complementary bipolar process and voltage-feedback topology.
Added datasheet revisions: Rev 0 (date unknown), A 9/02, B 5/05, C 8/11.
Added PCN 14_0246 (MSOP assembly-site addition, ASE Chungli); assembly, not die, change.
